title: Mouni Roy and Suraj Nambiar Confirmed Their Split — Then Followed Each Other Back on Instagram. What's Going On?
excerpt: The couple issued a joint statement on May 14 asking for privacy, unfollowed each other, and within 48 hours reconnected — leaving the diaspora's favourite TV-star-turned-Bollywood-actor's personal life more confusing than a Naagin plot twist
body:
Two weeks of furious speculation ended on May 14 when Mouni Roy and Dubai-based entrepreneur Suraj Nambiar posted a joint statement on Instagram confirming they had "decided to part ways." The wording was deliberate, almost lawyerly: they asked media to stop "sensationalised" coverage and said they were "taking time to address matters privately and amicably."

Within hours of the announcement, eagle-eyed fans noticed the couple had unfollowed each other — the modern-day equivalent of removing your wedding ring. Mouni's comments section flooded with heartbreak emojis and pleas from fans across India, the US, and the Gulf.

Then the plot twisted.

Less than 48 hours after confirming their separation, both Mouni and Suraj quietly re-followed each other on Instagram. No explanation. No statement. Just a silent digital olive branch that sent entertainment media into a fresh frenzy.

The backstory NRIs need to know

Mouni Roy — known internationally for her role as Isha in Brahmastra opposite Ranbir Kapoor and domestically as the original Naagin — married Suraj Nambiar in a dreamy Goa ceremony in January 2022. Nambiar, a Bengaluru-born investment banker working in Dubai, represented the kind of cross-border NRI love story the diaspora adores. Their wedding featured both South Indian and Bengali rituals, reflecting the couple's multicultural backgrounds.

For NRIs who watched Mouni rise from Ekta Kapoor's television universe to a genuine Bollywood presence — Gold with Akshay Kumar, Made in China with Rajkumari Rao — the marriage felt like a fairytale continuation.

What the Instagram breadcrumbs suggest

Crucially, Mouni has not deleted her wedding photos from Instagram — a detail fans have latched onto as evidence the split may not be final. Multiple Indian entertainment outlets report that the couple's friends describe the situation as a "cooling-off period" rather than a clean break.

The re-follow is doing heavy lifting in the rumour mill. Optimistic fans see it as reconciliation. Sceptics call it mature co-existence. Either way, the story isn't over.

Why this matters beyond Page 3

For the Indian diaspora, celebrity marriages serve as cultural touchstones. Mouni's Goa wedding was aspirational for NRI couples navigating intercultural relationships. The public messiness of the split — the unfollows, the joint statement, the instant reversal — mirrors the very modern challenge of conducting private life under a social-media microscope.

The couple has requested privacy, and fans across Mumbai, Dubai, New York, and London are — for once — largely respecting that. Whether the re-follow signals reconciliation or simply two adults choosing to be decent to each other online, it's a story the diaspora will be watching closely.
